div.head: Hl 11
div.ab: Gif man mannan an oþres flette manswara hateþ oððe hine mid bismærwordum scandlice grete, scilling agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI scill' þam þe he þæt word togecwæde, ⁊ cyninge XII scll' forgelde.
Gif man mannan an oþres flette manswara hateþ oððe hine mid bismærwordum scandlice grete, scilling agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI scill' þam þe he þæt word to gecwæde, ⁊ cyninge XII scll' forgelde.
Gif man mannan an oþres flette manswara hateþ oððe hine mid bismærwordum scandlice grete, scilling agelde þam þe þæt flet age, ⁊ VI sciƚƚ þam þe he þæt word togecwæde, ⁊ cyninge XII scƚƚ forgelde.

Wenn einer jemanden in eines andren Hause ‘Meineidiger’ heisst oder ihn mit Schimpfworten schändlich anfährt, so gelte er [1] Schilling demjenigen, der das Haus besitzt und 6 Schill. demjenigen, dem er jenes Wort zurief und dem König zahle er 12 Schilling.

If someone calls a person ‘perjurer’ in another’s house or rudely addresses him with abusive words, then let him pay [1] shilling to the one who owns the house and 6 shillings to the one to whom he called out that word, and let him pay the king 12 shillings.

If one man calls another a perjurer in a third man’s house, or accosts him abusively with insulting words, he shall pay one shilling to him who owns the house, 6 shillings to him he has accosted, and 12 shillings to the king.

If anyone in another’s house calls a man a perjurer, or shamefully accosts him with insulting words, he is to pay a shilling to him who owns the house, and six shillings to him to whom he spoke that word, and to pay 12 shillings to the king.

If a person in another’s house calls a person a perjurer or accosts him shamefully with mocking words, let him pay a shilling to him who owns that house, and 6 shillings to him to whom he spoke that utterance, and let him pay 12 shillings to the king.

note.seg: Die Sätze 11—15 bilden wieder Einen Abschnitt von Schutzrecht und Haftung des Hausherrn für den Hausfrieden (s. d. Gl 2a) bzw. den Friedbruch durch Hausgenossen. In c. 11f. handelt es sich um Ehrenkränkung (s. d. Gl 7f.), in 12ff., aber vielleicht auch schon in 11, ums Biergelage; s. d. Gl 7b

Clauses 11—15 again form a single section, on the protection-right of the master of the house and his liability for the peace of the house (see that word in Gl 2a) or for breach of the peace by members of his household. In c. 11f. the matter is insult to honour (see that word in Gl 7f.), in 12ff., but perhaps already in 11, the drinking-party; see that word in Gl 7b
Flett (s. Wb) ist das Haus (s. d. Gl 1e) des Gemeinfreien, nicht gerade niederen Ranges, wie Price nur aus der nach-Agsä. Zeit annimmt
Flett (see Wb) is the house (see that word in Gl 1e) of the common freeman, not specifically of one of lower rank, as Price assumes solely on the basis of the post-A.-S. period
Über den Nominativ s. Grimm Kl. Schr. V 320. Der Ausdruck Meineid (s. d. Gl 2. 8) umfasst auch Versprechensbruch
On the nominative see Grimm Kl. Schr. V 320. The term perjury (see that word in Gl 2. 8) also covers breach of promise
‘Anreden’ ist die Grundbed. im Germanischen, die ursprünglich auch feindlichen Sinn nicht ausschliesst; s. Kluge Etym. Wb. s. v. ‘Gruss’
‘Address’ is the basic meaning in Germanic, which originally does not exclude a hostile sense either; see Kluge Etym. Wb. s. v. ‘Gruss’
Der Hausherr empfängt die Busse für voll gebrochenen Schutz (s. d. Gl 15) nur bei Blutvergiessen u. 14²
The master of the house receives the compensation for fully broken protection (see that word in Gl 15) only in the case of bloodshed, below 14²
Die Ehre wird also dem Schutz gleich gewertet. Später verschmelzen beide Begriffe
Honour is thus valued equally with protection. Later the two concepts merge
The same fixed fine (see above 9²) also below 12f.
Cf. Seebohm, Tribal Custom in A.S. Law, p. 240.
